summary: When the project has an approved Process Policy, `backlog_compile.py approve` records its path, revision and source hash, the pin a Delivery takes at scope approval, in `backlog.md` and in each review note it approves, so a backlog revision and its reviews outside any Delivery name the process switch values they ran under. The pin follows `approved_at_utc` and sits inside the notes' source and package hashes. It is a record and is never compared: a later policy revision leaves the approved backlog current, a review approved earlier keeps its own pin, and `begin-revision` drops the pin from the new draft until its own approval. A draft or invalid policy refuses a new approval before any write; re-approving an unchanged approved backlog is unaffected. Without a policy nothing is recorded, and a new golden all-default approval run proves every backlog file the approval writes byte-identical to the previous release apart from #306's legacy story fix. The `story_size_budget` instructions now leave the policy revision to that record and keep only the limits in an epic review's Slicing evidence.
